chunks: Hishām ibn Sālim narrated from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
“The believer remains in a state of latitude within his religion so long as he does not shed unlawful blood.”
And he said: “The intentional killer of a believer is not granted success for repentance.”

key_terms.الْمُؤْمِنُ: the believer, whose life is inviolable in this context
key_terms.دَمًا حَرَامًا: unlawful blood, meaning bloodshed that is forbidden
key_terms.فِي فُسْحَةٍ مِنْ دِينِهِ: in a state of latitude and room within his religion
key_terms.قَاتِلُ الْمُؤْمِنِ مُتَعَمِّدًا: one who deliberately kills a believer
key_terms.لِلتَّوْبَةِ: for repentance; being granted success to truly repent

ai.seo_question: What does this hadith say about unlawfully killing a believer and repentance?
ai.summary: This hadith warns that a believer remains within the scope of religious safety so long as he does not commit the shedding of unlawful blood. It also emphasizes the grave danger of intentionally killing a believer, describing such a person as not being granted divine success to repent.
